insights.insight: $4.68M in cryptographically verified purchase GMV across 88,121+ receipts establishes a deterministic data asset — not modeled, not inferred. At ~455 receipts/day structural pace, the dataset is compounding faster than most brand-side measurement teams can act on.

The industry pays $5+ CPM to infer purchase intent from behavioral signals; a verified receipt confirms a transaction happened, at a specific retailer, for a specific amount. That gap — inference versus proof — is the core arbitrage available to brands willing to work with receipt-level data.

insights.topic: Rolling 7-day GMV ceiling: $101K crossed three times
insights.insight: The trailing 7-day window has cleared $101K on three consecutive pre-rollover readings (Oct 5, 6, 9), with post-rollover floors holding consistently in the $82–86K range — a mechanical UTC artifact, not demand softness. The floor is rising alongside the ceiling, signaling genuine throughput growth rather than volatility.

insights.topic: Grocery dominates but category spread is real
insights.insight: Grocery-supermarkets lead at 28.2% of 14-day receipts, but restaurants-dining (21.8%), retail-department-stores (17.2%), and gas-convenience are all structurally present — this is a four-category dataset, not a single-vertical panel, which expands its utility for cross-category brand measurement.

insights.topic: Brand-level receipt visibility: Kroger holds over Costco, Whole Foods emerging
insights.insight: In the 14-day window, Kroger (173 receipts) has widened its gap over Costco (127 receipts), while Whole Foods crossed the visibility threshold for the first time on Oct 9 — structural status pending, but the direction is toward premium grocery representation alongside mass-market chains.

insights.topic: BTC-denominated incentive layer with dollar-stable payout logic
insights.insight: Consumer incentives are paid in sats at 122 sats/receipt, with the rate inverse-adjusted to BTC price (~$82,186) to hold dollar-denominated payout value roughly stable — meaning the incentive mechanism is designed to be price-agnostic to consumers, which reduces churn risk tied to crypto volatility.
